lessons.pray: Risen Lord, thank you for conquering death and making my labour in you not in vain. When projects are cancelled and effort goes unseen, make me steadfast and immovable. Help me leave the results to you and keep faithfulness as my part. Today I want to abound in your work, because you remember all that I do. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Give the Lord one piece of work that feels ‘wasted’
Encourage a colleague whose recent effort came to nothing
Memorise 1 Corinthians 15:58 and recite it when you save a file
lessons.noon: “Your labour is not in vain in the Lord” — Lord, right now I let go of the results and keep working faithfully.

lessons.title: Show Home of the New Creation
lessons.theme: There is work in God’s kingdom; today’s faithfulness is a foretaste

v: They will build houses and inhabit them. They will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
They will not build and another inhabit. They will not plant and another eat; for the days of my people will be like the days of a tree, and my chosen will long enjoy the work of their hands.
They will not labour in vain nor give birth for calamity; for they are the offspring of the LORD’s blessed and their descendants with them.
The nations will walk in its light. The kings of the earth bring the glory and honour of the nations into it.
Its gates will in no way be shut by day (for there will be no night there),
and they shall bring the glory and the honour of the nations into it so that they may enter.

lessons.still: Before you begin work today, imagine: in God’s perfect kingdom, what would this job look like? Say, “Lord, let today’s work be a small foretaste of your kingdom.”
teach: Isaiah saw the new heavens and new earth: “They will build houses and inhabit them. They will plant vineyards and eat their fruit” (Isaiah 65:21). “They will not labour in vain” (Isaiah 65:23). There, work is not abolished but healed: no stolen results, no wasted sweat. Revelation adds that “the kings of the earth bring the glory and honour of the nations into it”, and “they shall bring the glory and the honour of the nations into it” (Revelation 21:24, 26). The good fruits of human culture, purified, will be carried into the new city.

People buying off-plan homes often visit the show home first. The building isn’t finished, but the show home lets you see what is coming: the layout, the light, the finish. A Christian’s work is like a show home of God’s kingdom. When you keep honest accounts, care for patients wholeheartedly or treat employees fairly, you give the world an early look at the kingdom where no one labours in vain.

Over these four weeks we have travelled from creation to new creation: God is the first worker, and we are called to cultivate and keep; sin brought toil and Babel, but Christ has redeemed our labour and promised a kingdom to come. Change your thinking and your life changes: work is not a temporary chore but a rehearsal for the eternal kingdom. Let Jesus be King, starting at today’s desk; one day we shall reign with him.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One purpose — to build God’s order. Overcomers will one day sit with Christ on his throne and reign with him; faithfulness at work today is rehearsal for that day. A change of perspective: from the temporary to the eternal.
lessons.scene: Lin Zixuan is a kitchen apprentice at a restaurant in Taipei. At twenty-three he spends his days chopping onions, scrubbing pans and prepping until late at night. His family often say, ‘You went to university to become a kitchen hand?’ Today the head chef has let him cook the staff meal for the first time. He stares at the leftovers in the fridge, torn between ‘just throw something together’ and ‘cook a really good dish’.
q: Who is God? — In the new heavens and earth, God still has people building and planting. How does he value our work?
Who am I? — What kind of ‘show home’ of the kingdom could your work be today?
How shall I respond? — If you were Zixuan, how could that staff meal become a foretaste of the kingdom?
lessons.jesus: The risen Jesus made breakfast on the beach for his weary disciples: “Come and eat breakfast!” (John 21:12). In his risen body he still lit a fire, prepared fish and bread and served others. That breakfast was a show home of the new creation: in his kingdom, work and service are made new, full of love and joy.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for promising new heavens and a new earth, where we will not labour in vain. Let my work today be a show home of your kingdom: honest, wholehearted and full of love. When others look down on my work, remind me that you value it. Let me learn here to reign with you, until the day you return. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Finish one small task to a ‘kingdom show home’ standard
Spend one minute praying for what your industry looks like in God’s kingdom
Looking back over four weeks, write down one changed belief
lessons.noon: “They will not labour in vain” — Lord, right now, here, I work for your kingdom.

mem.t: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

lessons.title: Dragging My Box to the Top
lessons.theme: Pride is leaving my place and grabbing power that isn't mine

v: How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of the dawn! How you are cut down to the ground, who laid the nations low!
You said in your heart, “I will ascend into heaven! I will exalt my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north!
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!”
Yet you shall be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.
who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men.
And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross.

lessons.still: Sit down and rest your open hands on your knees. Say to the Lord: “Lord, today I won't sit in your seat. You are God and I am not; you are King and I am your servant.” Take one more slow breath before you switch on your computer.
teach: Isaiah 14 is a lament over the king of Babylon, and many interpreters through the centuries have also heard in it the pattern of every proud fall. Listen to the heart speaking: “I will ascend into heaven! I will exalt my throne above the stars of God!” and then, “I will make myself like the Most High!” Five times in two verses it says, “I will.” Pride is not simply confidence. It is the creature leaving its place to climb onto the Creator's throne. The ending comes quickly: “Yet you shall be brought down to Sheol.” Those who climb hardest fall deepest.

Open any company's organisation chart. Everyone has a box, and lines connect the boxes. Pride is like someone quietly editing the file late at night and dragging their own box to the very top. The job title hasn't changed, but in the heart a coronation has taken place: my decisions need no consultation, my credit needs no sharing, and other people are simply tools. You can edit a company chart, but the universe has only one Chief Executive. When one person leaves their place, the whole chart goes wrong, departments start to grind against each other and the team loses its order.

Philippians 2 paints the opposite picture. Jesus, “existing in the form of God, didn't consider equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself.” The fallen one grasped upwards; Jesus willingly stepped down. This is what 321 teaches: pride is leaving your place to seize power; humility is laying power down and returning to your place, letting people be people and letting God be God. Change your thinking and your life changes. Today you don't need to fight for that top box. It was never yours, and only he can sit there securely.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Self-centredness means wanting to be lord and king, wanting to replace God, and it is the root of every fall. Letting Jesus be King begins with admitting, “That seat is his.” When we return to our place, we finally find rest.
lessons.scene: Jiahao is a project manager at a software company, sharp and quick. In this week's requirements meeting he spots a flaw in his manager's plan, and a thought rises: “I'll just email the managing director directly and show everyone who should really be making the call.” His cursor is already hovering over “Send”.
q: Who is God? — From the fall of the proud one and the self-emptying of Jesus, whose throne do you see it is?
Who am I? — In your workplace, where are you most tempted to quietly drag your own box upwards?
How shall I respond? — If you were Jiahao, how could you speak the truth without leaving your place?
lessons.jesus: Jesus is the only one who truly belongs at the top, yet he came down of his own accord, “taking the form of a servant,” and humbled himself all the way to the cross. He did not grab the throne, and the Father exalted him. He came down so that he could carry us, the fallen, back to our place.
lessons.pray: Most High Lord, I confess that the voice of “I will” is loud in me: I want to be seen, I want the final say, I want to be above others. Forgive me for wanting your seat. Today, in meetings and in my inbox, remind me to return to my place and to speak the truth with respect. I choose to let you be King. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Before a meeting, pray: “Lord, you are King; I serve”
Before sending an important email, ask: am I overstepping?
Show genuine respect for one decision by a manager or colleague
lessons.noon: “emptied himself, taking the form of a servant” — Lord, right now I lay down my urge to climb and bow low before you.

lessons.title: Did I Build Great Babylon?
lessons.theme: Whoever claims the credit must learn that the Most High rules

v: The king spoke and said, “Is not this great Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”
While the word was in the king’s mouth, a voice came from the sky, saying, “O King Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: ‘The kingdom has departed from you.

You shall be driven from men, and your dwelling shall be with the animals of the field. You shall be made to eat grass like oxen. Seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will.’”

This was fulfilled the same hour on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men and ate grass like oxen; and his body was wet with the dew of the sky until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.

At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me; and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honoured him who lives forever, for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom from generation to generation.

All the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing; and he does according to his will in the army of heaven, and amongst the inhabitants of the earth; and no one can stop his hand, or ask him, “What are you doing?”

At the same time my understanding returned to me; and for the glory of my kingdom, my majesty and brightness returned to me. My counsellors and my lords sought me; and I was established in my kingdom, and excellent greatness was added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honour the King of heaven; for all his works are truth, and his ways justice; and those who walk in pride he is able to abase.

lessons.still: Stand by a window or in the lift and glance at the city outside. Say quietly: “Lord, you hold all of this together. Whatever I build today, let it make you great.” Then turn your phone face down for thirty seconds.
teach: Nebuchadnezzar walked on the roof of his palace, surveying the city he had expanded, and said, “Is not this great Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?” While the words were still in his mouth, a voice came from the sky. The emperor was driven out to live with the animals and ate grass like oxen, until he knew “that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men.” At the end of that time he lifted his eyes to heaven and his understanding returned. His closing testimony is: “those who walk in pride he is able to abase.”

When a new building opens, there is often a stone plaque in the lobby: “Erected by Chairman So-and-so.” The plaque isn't wrong. The question is what is carved on the plaque in your heart. The self-centred person engraves their own name on every achievement: I hit the target, I rescued the project, I hold this company together. But the bricklayer's sweat, the designer's drawings, the accountant's ledgers, the cleaner's late-night mop, and the breath, health and timing God provides, have no names on that plaque. When the heart's plaque bears the wrong name, a person begins to lose their reason.

Nebuchadnezzar's turning point was when he “lifted up” his eyes “to heaven.” When his focus moved from himself to the Most High, his sanity came back. 321 says: keep your focus on Jesus, not on yourself. This doesn't mean pretending we contributed nothing. It means admitting, “what do you have that you didn't receive?” (1 Corinthians 4:7). People who give the credit to God do not shrink; like Nebuchadnezzar, they are established again. Letting Jesus receive all the glory is the healthiest view of success there is.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Shift your perspective — from the human view to God's view, from “I built this” to “he holds this up.” Letting Jesus receive all the glory is not a polite show of modesty; it is worship that comes from seeing things as they really are.
lessons.scene: Zhenhua runs a construction firm in Kuala Lumpur, and the first office tower his company has led is about to open. His secretary sends over the ribbon-cutting speech. Reading it, he counts the word “I” more than twenty times, while his site manager and team are not mentioned once. The ceremony is at nine tomorrow morning.
q: Who is God? — How does “the Most High rules in the kingdom of men” change the way you see your company, the market and your boss?
Who am I? — On your proudest achievement, whose name is carved on the plaque in your heart?
How shall I respond? — If you were Zhenhua, how would you rewrite that speech tonight?
lessons.jesus: Jesus did countless miracles, yet he said, “the Son can do nothing of himself” (John 5:19). He gave all the glory to the Father and let himself be misunderstood and crucified. The one who truly deserved a plaque chose instead to write our names on his heart.
lessons.pray: King of heaven, all your works are truth and your ways are just. I confess that I often treat your grace as my talent and my team's sweat as my achievement. Open my eyes so that I lift them to heaven. Today, over every result, I want to say: you held this up. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Write down three people behind a recent success of yours
Thank one of them publicly today, naming what they did
Write “The Most High rules” in today's calendar
lessons.noon: “those who walk in pride he is able to abase” — Lord, right now I lift my eyes to you and hand today's results back to you.

lessons.title: Five Faces of the Self
lessons.theme: Credit-grabbing, blame-shifting, comparing, controlling and pleasing all say, “I want to be king”

v: A dispute also arose amongst them, which of them was considered to be greatest.
He said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’
But not so with you. Rather, the one who is greater amongst you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves.
For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am amongst you as one who serves.
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.

lessons.still: Close your eyes and gently touch your face with your palm. Say to the Lord: “Lord, today I won't go to work wearing a mask. Show me what my heart is really like, and cover me with your love.”
teach: At the Last Supper, Jesus had just broken the bread and spoken of his body given and his blood poured out. Yet “a dispute also arose amongst” the disciples, “which of them was considered to be greatest.” Arguing about rankings at the holiest moment: that is the human heart. Jesus did not scold them. He simply asked, “who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves?” and then said, “I am amongst you as one who serves.” The Lord did not abolish greatness. He redefined it.

On video calls many people switch on a beauty filter. The self-centred life has five filters at work. The first is credit-grabbing, which filters the team's success into “me”. The second is blame-shifting, which filters my mistake into “them”. The third is comparison, always eyeing other people's salaries and desks. The fourth is control: everything must pass through my hands because I trust no one. The fifth is people-pleasing, gentle on the surface but really afraid of losing approval. Five faces that look different, but when the camera goes off they are one face: I want to be in charge.

Paul's prescription is: “in humility, each counting others better than himself; each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.” This is not self-contempt. It is moving the spotlight off ourselves. 321 says people matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than things. When I stop grabbing credit, colleagues are seen. When I stop shifting blame, the team feels safe. When I stop pleasing people, I can be honest. Recognising which face you wear most often is where change begins.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-centred life shows itself as pride, and pride provokes pride until both sides lose; humility inspires humility until both sides win. Take off one mask today and let Jesus be King in you.
lessons.scene: Shihan is a planner at an advertising agency in Taipei. Today's pitch went brilliantly, and the client agreed on the spot. Back at the office her boss asks, “Whose idea was that key visual?” The spark actually came from a passing comment by Siti, the intern, who is sitting in the corner sorting files with her head down.
q: Who is God? — Jesus said, “I am amongst you as one who serves.” What kind of Lord do you see in that?
Who am I? — Credit-grabbing, blame-shifting, comparing, controlling, pleasing: which face do you know best?
How shall I respond? — If you were Shihan, how would you answer your boss in that moment?
lessons.jesus: On the night the disciples argued about who was greatest, Jesus took a towel, knelt down and washed their feet. He wore no masks: he did not grab credit, shift blame, compare, control or please. He had only one face, the face of a servant who loved to the end.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you see every face I wear in the meeting room. I confess that I want to be called great too, and I am afraid of my mistakes being seen. Forgive me. Give me courage to give credit to those who earned it and to carry my own responsibility. Today let me learn your way and serve among my colleagues. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Name the face you wear most and write it on a sticky note
Mention a colleague's contribution in front of others today
When you make a mistake, start with “That's on me”
lessons.noon: “I am amongst you as one who serves” — Lord, right now I lay down my need to be greatest and learn to serve like you.

lessons.title: The Top Seller and the Clean Room
lessons.theme: Strength is the most dangerous season; success tempts us to cross the line

v: In Jerusalem, he made devices, invented by skilful men, to be on the towers and on the battlements, with which to shoot arrows and great stones. His name spread far abroad, because he was marvellously helped until he was strong.
But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up, so that he did corruptly and he trespassed against the LORD his God, for he went into the LORD’s temple to burn incense on the altar of incense.
Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, who were valiant men.

They resisted Uzziah the king, and said to him, “It isn’t for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have trespassed. It will not be for your honour from the LORD God.”

Then Uzziah was angry. He had a censer in his hand to burn incense, and while he was angry with the priests, the leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the LORD’s house, beside the altar of incense.

Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, and behold, he was leprous in his forehead; and they thrust him out quickly from there. Indeed, he himself also hurried to go out, because the LORD had struck him.

lessons.still: Before work, bring to mind today's most important figure or result. Then say: “Lord, this is your help. Where I am strongest, keep me from crossing the line.” Rest in that for ten seconds before you head out.
teach: Uzziah became king at sixteen. At first he set himself to seek God, and God made him prosper: victories in battle, towers built, wells dug, farming flourishing, even new war machines made by skilled craftsmen. Scripture says “he was marvellously helped until he was strong.” The next verse turns sharply: “But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up.” He marched into the temple to burn incense himself. Eighty priests tried to stop him, and he became angry. In that very moment of anger, leprosy broke out on his forehead, and he was cut off from the house of the LORD.

High-tech factories have clean rooms. Whoever you are, you must put on a clean suit and pass through an air shower before you enter. Imagine a manager who has topped the sales chart three years running. He thinks changing is a waste of time for someone of his importance and strides straight in, and an entire batch of silicon wafers is ruined. Uzziah's problem was not weakness but strength, so much strength that he assumed the rules were for other people. Success brings its own great temptation: the feeling that “I can be the exception.”

The key words in Uzziah's tragedy are “when he was strong” and “angry.” When the self-centred are corrected, they do not examine themselves; they are provoked. When the humble are stopped, they pause and ask whether God might be speaking through someone. 321 says pride is leaving your place to seize power. A king has a king's place and a priest has a priest's place. The more successful we are, the more we need to remember that we were “marvellously helped.” People who remember they have been helped don't cross the line.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-centred life often appears not in failure but in success. Letting Jesus be King means that even at my strongest I gladly keep my place, accept correction and stay within the boundaries God has set.
lessons.scene: Wei Jie is a relationship manager at a bank in Singapore and has been top performer three years running. Today a major client urgently wants a new account opened, but compliance review will take three days. He thinks, “With my numbers, I'll open it now and file the documents later. Who's going to argue?” His compliance colleague's phone is ringing.
q: Who is God? — From Uzziah's story, what do you see about how God regards a heart after he has blessed it?
Who am I? — Which recent success has started to make you feel you can be the exception?
How shall I respond? — If you were Wei Jie, what would you say when your compliance colleague picks up?
lessons.jesus: Jesus is the true High Priest and the King of kings. He had every right to enter the Most Holy Place, yet he humbly followed the path the Father set, step by step to the cross. Uzziah tried to force his way into the temple with power; Jesus opened a new way into God's presence for us with his own blood.
lessons.pray: God who helps me, every result I have comes from you. Keep me from a proud heart in my season of strength. When colleagues, rules or managers stop me, help me not to get angry but to pause and examine myself. Today I choose to stay within the lines at every step of the process. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Name one “do it now, sort it later” shortcut you've been eyeing
Follow one procedure today that you usually find tedious
When someone corrects you, begin with “Thanks for the reminder”
lessons.noon: “But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up” — Lord, right now I remember that I am someone you have helped. Guard my heart.

lessons.title: Water Flows Downhill
lessons.theme: God resists the proud, and grace flows to the humble heart

v: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
Lament, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom.
Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.

lessons.still: Plant your feet on the floor and lower your head a little. Say to the Lord: “Lord, I humble myself before you. Today I won't lift myself up; I only ask for your grace to flow in.” Take three breaths before you start work.
teach: James 4 begins by exposing the roots of conflict, in the workplace and in the church: selfish desire, envy and rivalry. Then comes this week's memory verse: “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.” The word for “resists” comes from the language of battle, an army drawn up in opposition. The proud don't merely miss out on blessing; they put themselves in opposition to God. Yet the same verse says, “he gives more grace.” A string of commands follows: submit to God, resist the devil, draw near to God, cleanse your hands, purify your hearts. And finally: “Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.”

Every builder knows that water flows downhill. In heavy rain the high ground stays dry and the water collects in the low places. God's grace is like water. A proud heart is like a raised platform that cannot hold rain no matter how hard it falls. A humble heart is like a dug-out reservoir, and grace runs into it naturally. When you admit a mistake to your manager, step down from your position with a customer, or say sorry first to a colleague, you are not becoming smaller. You are digging deeper and making room for grace.

321 says humility is the key to revival. Personal revival, team revival and company revival all begin when someone is willing to bow their head. Humility inspires humility: a manager who apologises first often receives honesty from the team. Pride provokes pride: one blunt email only invites a blunter reply. Looking back over this week, we have seen the five faces of the self and the falls of Nebuchadnezzar and Uzziah. Today, let us choose the low place. That is where the grace is.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is the key to revival. Humility is laying down power and returning to your place, letting people be people and God be God. Humility inspires humility and both win; pride provokes pride and both lose.
lessons.scene: Shufen is a nurse unit manager at a hospital in Taichung. Last week she clashed with the emergency department's unit manager in a handover meeting, and now the two units barely speak; patient transfers keep getting stuck. This morning, carrying two coffees, she sees the other manager coming towards her down the corridor, and her steps slow.
q: Who is God? — God “resists the proud” and “gives more grace”: how do both belong together in him?
Who am I? — This week, in which working relationship have you seen yourself standing on high ground?
How shall I respond? — If you were Shufen, how would you be the first to bow your head in that corridor?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “I am gentle and humble in heart” (Matthew 11:29). He was the highest of all, yet he went to the lowest places: a manger, a cross, a tomb. And God exalted him to the highest place. Every low place he walked through became a channel for grace to flow to us.
lessons.pray: Gracious Lord, I confess that I often stand on high ground waiting for others to bow first. Soften my heart so that I humble myself before you. Today, in that frozen relationship, give me courage to take the first step and say the first kind word. Let your grace flow from the low places into my department and my team. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Memorise James 4:6 and set it as your lock screen
Greet a colleague you're at odds with, first, today
Apologise briefly and sincerely for one small thing you got wrong
lessons.noon: “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble” — Lord, right now I choose the low place. Let your grace flow in.

mem.t: But seek first Gods Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

lessons.title: Tonight's Cloud Account
lessons.theme: Those who store up treasure for themselves cannot even keep themselves

v: He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’
He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.”’
“But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich towards God.”

lessons.still: Pick up your phone and glance at today's calendar. Then say to the Lord: “Lord, my life doesn't consist in the abundance of my possessions. Every hour today is on loan from you.” Put the phone back in your pocket and take one deep breath.
teach: Jesus told a parable about a rich man whose land produced so much that he had nowhere to store it. He held a meeting with himself and concluded: “I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones,” and then tell his soul to take its ease, eat, drink and be merry. Notice that in this whole speech there is no God, no neighbour and no family; only my crops, my barns, my grain, my soul. God says just one thing: “You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?”

Today our barns are not beside the fields but in the cloud. Photos, sales reports, savings, contacts, a polished CV. When space runs out we upgrade the plan: from 50 GB to 2 TB, then to unlimited. We assume more capacity means more security, forgetting that the account holder may be logged out tonight. The rich man's mistake was not wealth or good planning. It was saving his whole life onto a drive he could not take with him, while he was “not rich towards God.”

Before the parable Jesus says, “a man's life doesn't consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.” That is a change of perspective: from the earthly to the heavenly, from the temporary to the eternal. Being rich towards God means investing time, money and ability in loving God and loving people: a dinner with the family, support for a struggling colleague, a quiet gift no one sees. 321 says relationships matter more than things. Don't tear down your most precious relationships just to build bigger barns.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Shift your perspective from the temporary to the eternal. Relationships matter more than things, so never damage a relationship for the sake of things. Being rich towards God is the one account that can never be logged out.
lessons.scene: Ah Chang runs a seafood restaurant in Penang, and business is so good he is opening a third branch. He spreads out next year's plan: visiting the branches seven days a week, meeting suppliers on Sundays, checking the accounts every night. His wife says quietly, “And Sunday worship? The children's parents' evening?” His pen stops over the Sunday column.
q: Who is God? — God said, “tonight your soul is required of you.” What does that show you about God and your life?
Who am I? — Which barn are you most eager to “build bigger” right now?
How shall I respond? — If you were Ah Chang, how would you rearrange that Sunday column?
lessons.jesus: Jesus is Lord of heaven and earth, yet he had “nowhere to lay his head” (Matthew 8:20). He built no barns, yet he poured out his whole life and stored up for us a treasure that never perishes. He became poor so that through his poverty we might become rich.
lessons.pray: Lord who gives life, I confess that I often think only of expanding my barns and forget that you can call my life back at any moment. Teach me to be rich towards you, to keep time for my family and my heart for you. Today, in every budget line and calendar slot, help me ask first what you want. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Block out undisturbed family time in this week's calendar first
Quietly do something for a colleague today, expecting nothing back
Before leaving work, ask: was I rich towards God today?
lessons.noon: “a man's life doesn't consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses” — Lord, right now I let go of my anxiety for more and rest in being rich towards you.

lessons.title: Life on a Treadmill
lessons.theme: Labour without God, however fast, only runs on the spot

v: Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labour and chasing after wind.
Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun.

There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labour, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then do I labour and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labour in vain. Unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.
It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

lessons.still: Sit up and place both hands on your chest. Feel your heartbeat. Say to the Lord: “Lord, you gave me this heart. Today I won't work myself ragged to prove myself. I want to work from rest in you.”
teach: The Teacher observes a man who “is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labour, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth.” In the end the man asks himself, “For whom then do I labour and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” He is not lazy; he is too industrious. He is not without achievements; his achievements cannot fill his heart. The Teacher's conclusion is very plain: “Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labour and chasing after wind.”

A gym treadmill is an honest machine. You can adjust the speed and the incline and run for an hour dripping with sweat, and when you step off you are exactly where you started. A workaholic's life is much like a treadmill. The targets keep rising and the salary keeps growing, yet when we look up we are still in the same place: just as anxious, just as lonely, just as unsatisfied. The psalm says, “Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labour in vain.” Without God, however fast we run, we are running on the spot.

Psalm 127 goes on: “for he gives sleep to his loved ones.” This does not encourage idleness. It means that the beloved don't need to earn their worth by toil. 321 says: rely on the Holy Spirit with your heart, not on yourself with your head. Living from the heart brings joy; living from the head brings worry. Workaholism is often an attempt to replace God's approval with results. Today we can step off the treadmill, come to God, and hear him say: you are my beloved.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Self-centred labour tries to prove itself; self-emptied work responds to his love. Rely on the Spirit with your heart, not on yourself with your head; with your focus on Jesus, a handful with quietness is enough.
lessons.scene: Rachel is a senior associate at a law firm in Auckland, pushing hard for partnership. At eleven at night she is eating a cold takeaway dinner at her desk when her mum's message pops up: “Coming home for dinner this weekend?” She glances at the four contracts still waiting for review.
q: Who is God? — “He gives sleep to his loved ones.” What does that show you about how God sees your labour?
Who am I? — If the Teacher asked you, “For whom then do I labour?”, how would you answer?
How shall I respond? — If you were Rachel, how would you reply to your mum's message?
lessons.jesus: Jesus' three years of ministry were extremely busy; crowds pressed in so that he hardly had time to eat. Yet the Gospel records: “Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there” (Mark 1:35). His work flowed not from pressure but from communion with the Father.
lessons.pray: Dear Father, I confess that I often run hard on the treadmill, trying to prove my worth through results. Help me stop and hear you say that I am your beloved. Today help me work wholeheartedly and also rest at the right time, honouring the family and the body you have given me. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Set an alarm to leave work on time today, and keep it
Reply to a family message and fix a time to meet
Before bed, commit tomorrow to God and stay off work email
lessons.noon: “Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labour and chasing after wind” — Lord, right now I slow down and find quietness in you.

lessons.title: Thirty-Seven Open Tabs
lessons.theme: In all the busyness, only one thing is needed

v: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet and heard his word.
But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.”
Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”

lessons.still: Close the extra windows on your phone and computer and leave just one open. Say to the Lord: “Lord, many things are waiting for me today, but one thing is needed. Let me sit at your feet for one minute first.” Count sixty seconds in silence.
teach: Martha welcomed Jesus into her home, a lovely act of service. But Scripture says “Martha was distracted with much serving,” and eventually she complained to Jesus: “Lord, don't you care that my sister left me to serve alone?” Jesus gently said her name twice: “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.” Jesus did not criticise the cooking. He pointed to a heart pulled in many directions.

How many tabs are open in your browser right now? Many people count and find thirty-seven: email, reports, a shopping basket, a school notice, unanswered group chats. Every tab eats memory, the computer slows to a crawl and finally freezes. Martha's heart had too many tabs open: the food wasn't ready, the guests were waiting, her sister wasn't helping, and the Lord didn't seem to care. Busyness is not sin, but when busyness pulls us away from Jesus' feet, even our service turns into complaint.

The “good part” Mary chose was not avoiding work. It was being with the Lord first and working afterwards. 321 says: life first, then relationships, then ministry. When the order is right, work does not become a crushing weight. This is true for homemakers, office workers and entrepreneurs alike. Before you open those thirty-seven tabs, open the most important one, your relationship with Jesus. No manager, client or deadline can take that good part away.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Life first, then relationships, then ministry. The order of relationships is God, self, others, tasks. When tasks jump to first place, the heart is in turmoil; when Jesus returns to first place, everything else finds its place.
lessons.scene: Xiulan is a stay-at-home mum in New Taipei who takes baking orders to help with the family income. The week before the Mid-Autumn Festival, orders explode and her kitchen is piled with mooncake moulds. Her youngest daughter comes in holding a children's Bible: “Mummy, can you read me one story?” At that moment the oven timer goes off.
q: Who is God? — Jesus said “Martha, Martha” twice. What kind of Lord do you hear in that gentle tone?
Who am I? — Which tabs are open in your heart right now, leaving you anxious and troubled?
How shall I respond? — If you were Xiulan, how would you answer your daughter as the timer rings?
lessons.jesus: Jesus did not lose his temper at Martha's complaint, nor did he think Mary rude for sitting. He valued people above a table of food. This same Lord is in your kitchen and your office today, gently calling your name and inviting you to his feet first.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you know how many things I have to do today and how often my heart is in turmoil. Call my name and bring me back to your feet. I choose the good part first, and then I will face the orders, the reports and the housework. In my busyness, help me not to forget the people beside me, because they matter more than tasks. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Read one verse of Scripture before opening your inbox
Close three unnecessary tabs or notifications today
Give someone near you ten phone-free minutes
lessons.noon: “one thing is needed” — Lord, right now I switch off the noise inside me and come back to your feet.

lessons.title: Install the Operating System First
lessons.theme: Seek first God's Kingdom and his righteousness; order decides everything

v: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.

lessons.still: Run through today's to-do list in your mind, then say: “Lord, before all of this I seek first your Kingdom and your righteousness. Today you come first.” Draw a small cross at the top of your list.
teach: In the Sermon on the Mount Jesus looked at people worried about making ends meet and said, “don't be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?', ‘What will we drink?' or, ‘With what will we be clothed?'” Not because these things don't matter, but because “your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.” Then comes this week's memory verse: “But seek first God's Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.” The key word is “first.” Jesus is not telling us to seek the Kingdom instead of working; he is putting things in order.

Every IT engineer knows that a new computer needs its operating system installed first; only then can you add applications. Treat the operating system as one more app and install it last, and the whole machine won't run. God's Kingdom is not an app in our lives, opened on Sunday and closed on Monday. It is the operating system. Work, income, family and hobbies are programmes that run on it. With the right order, every programme runs smoothly; with the wrong order, even the best software crashes.

To “seek first God's Kingdom” is to let Jesus be King. To seek “his righteousness” is to do things his way. 321 says: let Jesus be King and build God's order. This is not an abstract idea. It happens in daily choices: whom we consult first about the budget, whom we schedule first, whom we listen to first in a conflict. Jesus also says, “Each day's own evil is sufficient.” Entrusting tomorrow to the Father and working wholeheartedly in his Kingdom today is the rhythm of an overcomer.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One purpose — to build God's order. Letting Jesus be King is not adding one more religious activity to life; it is reordering the whole of life: God, self, others, tasks.
lessons.scene: Hongren is the plant manager of a metalworking factory in Tainan. A client has added a rush order, and the sales manager wants the whole plant working this Sunday. Hongren knows this is the weekend of his church's small-group leader training, and that the workers have already done overtime three weeks in a row. The sales manager messages again: “Boss, I need an answer.”
q: Who is God? — “Your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.” How does this help you know the Father?
Who am I? — In your life, is God's Kingdom more like the operating system, or an app you open now and then?
How shall I respond? — If you were Hongren, what reply would truly seek first God's Kingdom and his righteousness?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to accomplish his work” (John 4:34). The order of his life never slipped: first the Father's will, then his own needs. In Gethsemane he prayed, “not my will, but yours, be done,” and accomplished the greatest righteousness for us.
lessons.pray: Father, you know everything I need. Forgive me for so often ranking work, income and other people's expectations above you. Today I want to seek first your Kingdom and your righteousness, and to ask what you want in every choice. Give me wisdom to make a God-fearing decision between my company's needs and your will. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Make the first item on today's list: “Pray and commit”
For a stuck decision, ask: what do his Kingdom and righteousness require?
Write down one worry about tomorrow, give it to God, cross it out
lessons.noon: “seek first God's Kingdom and his righteousness” — Lord, right now I put you back in first place.

lessons.title: Taking Down the Trophy Wall
lessons.theme: Lift success off the altar and place it back in God's hands

v: That same night, the LORD said to him, “Take your father’s bull, even the second bull seven years old, and throw down the altar of Baal that your father has, and cut down the Asherah that is by it.
Then build an altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold, in an orderly way, and take the second bull, and offer a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah which you shall cut down.”
Then Gideon took ten men of his servants, and did as the LORD had spoken to him. Because he feared his father’s household and the men of the city, he could not do it by day, but he did it by night.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.

lessons.still: Look at the thing you are proudest of: a certificate, a sales figure, a job title or a piece of work. Say to the Lord: “Lord, you gave me this, but it is not my god. Today I place it back in your hands.”
teach: Before God called Gideon to rescue Israel, his first assignment was not the battlefield but his own home: “throw down the altar of Baal that your father has, and cut down the Asherah that is by it,” then build an altar to the LORD. Gideon was afraid and dared only to do it at night, but he “did as the LORD had spoken to him.” Before God uses a person, he first pulls down the idols in that person's house. The closing words of John's first letter say the same: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.”

Many offices and studies have a trophy wall: best salesperson, outstanding employee, innovation award of the year. Trophies are good, signs of the gifts and grace God has given. But when I need to look at them every day to feel I am worth something, when losing them would make life feel unbearable, that wall has become an altar. An idol is not only a statue in a temple. Anything that replaces God as the source of my security and identity can be a Baal.

Taking down the altar does not necessarily mean throwing the trophies away. It means, in the heart, moving them out of God's place. Gideon used the wood of the cut-down Asherah to offer a burnt offering to God. What had been worshipped became fuel for worshipping God. Success can be like that: from my idol to my offering. 321 says: let Jesus receive all the glory. This week we have met the rich fool, the workaholic and busy Martha. Today let us take down the wall in our hearts and place success back in God's hands.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let Jesus receive all the glory. When success becomes my god, I am ruling in self-centredness; when I offer success to God, it becomes building material for God's order.
lessons.scene: Jiaxin sells insurance in Kuala Lumpur and has won the company's top honour five years running; the wall behind her desk is covered in awards. This year her numbers have suddenly dropped. She has started losing sleep, and has even thought about overstating a policy's cover to a client. Her manager warns her: “A little lower and you'll miss this year's award.”
q: Who is God? — God had Gideon pull down the altar before going to battle. What does that show you about what God values?
Who am I? — What is the trophy wall in your life? If you lost it, would you still know who you are?
How shall I respond? — If you were Jiaxin, how would you place success back in God's hands when you meet your client today?
lessons.jesus: In the wilderness Satan showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, offering them all if he would bow down. Jesus refused and worshipped and served the Father alone. He would rather take the road to the cross than sit on a throne without the Father. His victory gives us the strength to pull down our idols.
lessons.pray: Only true God, I confess that I often enshrine success, targets and applause on the altar of my heart. Give me Gideon's obedience to do what you say even when I am afraid. I place my achievements and my failures in your hands and will no longer let them define me. May you receive all the glory in my work. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Name the achievement you most fear losing and pray over it
Be honest all the way in one matter today, whatever it costs
Memorise Matthew 6:33 and repeat it three times at lunch
lessons.noon: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols” — Lord, right now I hand you the trophy wall in my heart.

mem.t: I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.

lessons.title: The Offer Letter Before Day One
lessons.theme: Before I have done anything, the Father has already accepted me

v: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptised by him.
But John would have hindered him, saying, “I need to be baptised by you, and you come to me?”
But Jesus, answering, said to him, “Allow it now, for this is the fitting way for us to fulfil all righteousness.” Then he allowed him.
Jesus, when he was baptised, went up directly from the water: and behold, the heavens were opened to him. He saw the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming on him.
Behold, a voice out of the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”

lessons.still: Before work, simply listen to your breathing. Imagine the Father saying to you, “This is my beloved, with whom I am well pleased.” You don't need to answer; just receive it. Then say: “Lord, I take your pleasure with me to work.”
teach: Jesus was baptised in the Jordan. As he came up from the water, the heavens opened, the Spirit descended, and a voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.” Notice the timing. Jesus had not yet begun his public ministry. He had not done a single miracle or preached a single sermon. The Father's pleasure was not the reward for his work; it was the starting point of it. Straight afterwards Jesus was led into the wilderness to be tempted, and the devil's first words were, “If you are the Son of God.” The attack was aimed squarely at that identity.

Every new graduate remembers the moment the offer letter arrived. It was sent before your first day. The company was saying, “We have decided we want you.” You had achieved nothing yet, and you were already part of the team. But many people forget that letter once they start and live their whole career with a probation mindset, as though every review decides whether they deserve to stay. The good news of the gospel is that the Father's offer letter is not a probation contract. It is the status of a son or daughter.

If we try to earn identity through performance, performance takes us hostage: we grow proud when we do well and ashamed when we don't. These are the two faces of self-centredness. Jesus worked from the Father's pleasure, so he could face temptation without wavering, face crowds without pandering and face the cross without turning back. 321 says Jesus is my example. We too can go to work carrying the identity of the already accepted: not working in order to be loved, but working because we are loved. This is the first foundation stone of identity at work.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your thinking and your life changes — from “I only have value if I perform” to “I am already loved, so I go to work.” Only an identity rooted in Christ can live out the freedom of the self-emptied life.
lessons.scene: Tom is a new analyst in a government department in Wellington, and his three-month probation ends next week. Yesterday his manager sent back his report, asking him to rewrite two sections. This morning he stares at the screen while one thought loops in his head: “Maybe I'm just not cut out for this job.”
q: Who is God? — The Father said “with whom I am well pleased” before Jesus had done anything. What kind of Father do you see?
Who am I? — Do you often live with a probation mindset, trying to prove yourself before God and people?
How shall I respond? — If you were Tom, how would you rewrite that report as someone already accepted?
lessons.jesus: Jesus chose to stand in line with sinners to be baptised. He had nothing to repent of, yet he identified with us. Because he went into the water and onto the cross in our place, the words the Father spoke over him now reach us through him: we too are favoured “in the Beloved” (Ephesians 1:6).
lessons.pray: Father, thank you for loving and accepting me before I had achieved anything. I confess that I often measure my worth by results and by other people's opinions. Today help me remember your voice, and face every task and every revision with the security of being loved. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Write “I am the one the Father delights in” at the top of today's notes
Pray before you start revising a piece of returned work
Affirm something about a new colleague's character today
lessons.noon: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased” — Lord, right now I stop proving myself and rest in your pleasure.

lessons.title: The Old Me Has Handed Over
lessons.theme: Crucified with Christ, it is now Christ who lives in me

v: For I through the law died to the law, that I might live to God.

I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.
knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin.

lessons.still: Cross your arms over your chest like a cross. Say quietly: “Lord, the old me has been crucified with you. Today it is no longer I who live, but you who live in me.” Hold it for ten seconds, then lower your arms.
teach: Paul writes this week's memory verse: “I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.” He speaks of a completed fact, not “I must try hard to crucify myself” but “I have been.” Romans 6 says the same: “our old man was crucified with him.” In God's eyes the old self, centred on itself and determined to be lord and king, came to its end on the cross. The second half of the verse is even more moving: the Son of God “loved me and gave himself up for me.”

Anyone who has changed jobs has done a handover. You list the files, passwords, client contacts and unfinished tasks one by one and pass them to your successor. On the day the handover is complete, your name is removed from the system and the new person officially takes charge. The Christian life is a handover that has already been completed: the old self has resigned and Christ has taken over. Yet many of us go back to our old desk every day and give orders from our old account. Two systems clash, and we end up exhausted.

321 says the self-emptied life is not emptiness; it is entering and living out the infinite. “No longer I” does not cancel my personality or my gifts. It means I have a new owner. The old self lived on its own ability, its own reputation, its own plans. The new self lives “by faith in the Son of God.” When a colleague misunderstands me or a manager dismisses me, the old self rushes to defend itself. The new self can be still, because the “me” that needed protecting has already been handed over. That is real freedom.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-emptied life — “it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me” (Galatians 2:20). It is not disappearing but entering the infinite; self-denial means living for Jesus and for others, not for myself.
lessons.scene: Huimin teaches Chinese at a secondary school in Singapore. A parent has publicly accused her of favouritism in the class parents' chat and forwarded screenshots to the principal. She has already typed a long reply, every word of it reasonable, and her finger hovers over “Send”.
q: Who is God? — “who loved me and gave himself up for me.” How does this help you know the Christ who lives in you?
Who am I? — At work, when does your old self most often go back to its old desk and start giving orders?
How shall I respond? — If Christ were living in Huimin in that moment, how would she handle that message?
lessons.jesus: On the cross Jesus was insulted, misunderstood and condemned, yet he did not defend himself. He prayed for those who crucified him. It was not that he had no case; he had entrusted himself completely to the Father. He gave himself up so that our old self could die with him and our new life could come from him.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, who loved me and gave yourself up for me, thank you that my old self was crucified with you. I confess that I often go back to my old desk, anxious to protect my reputation. Today, when I face misunderstanding and criticism, live in me so that my words are gracious and my responses wise. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Memorise Galatians 2:20 and say it morning and lunchtime
When criticised, wait ten minutes before replying
In one matter, choose not to justify yourself and trust God
lessons.noon: “it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me” — Lord, right now I hand you my response to this moment.

lessons.title: Writing Off the CV
lessons.theme: Knowing Christ is the treasure; everything else is counted loss

v: though I myself might have confidence even in the flesh. If any other man thinks that he has confidence in the flesh, I yet more:
circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; concerning the law, a Pharisee;
concerning zeal, persecuting the assembly; concerning the righteousness which is in the law, found blameless.
However, I consider those things that were gain to me as a loss for Christ.

Yes most certainly, and I count all things to be a loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus, my Lord, for whom I suffered the loss of all things, and count them nothing but refuse, that I may gain Christ
and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own, that which is of the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness which is from God by faith,

lessons.still: Think of the title on your business card or the qualification you are proudest of. Then say to the Lord: “Lord, you gave me these, but you are worth far more. Today knowing you is my treasure.”
teach: Paul lists an enviable CV: “circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; concerning the law, a Pharisee,” zealous, and “found blameless.” In the Jewish world of his day this was a top university, a distinguished family and number one in the field all at once. Then he says, “However, I consider those things that were gain to me as a loss for Christ.” He even counts them “nothing but refuse, that I may gain Christ.”

Accountants know the balance sheet: assets on one side, liabilities on the other. Paul carried out an astonishing revaluation. Everything he once listed as an asset he wrote off as a loss. Not because those things were evil in themselves, but because next to Christ their value fell to zero. It is like a company acquiring a priceless patent; the old equipment is no longer its core asset. Once you have found the true treasure, the books must be redone.

Paul did not reject his education; he went on using it to preach the gospel. The point is that his righteousness and worth no longer came from his CV, but from “that which is through faith in Christ.” 321 says: shift your perspective from the worldly to the godly. Titles, degrees and seniority can become the armour of self-centredness, making us look down on others and live in fear of losing them. When Christ becomes our treasure, these things change from masters back into tools, and we can use them to serve people without being held hostage by them.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Shift your perspective from the worldly to the godly, from the temporary to the eternal. When Christ is my treasure, my job title no longer defines me; it becomes a tool for serving others.
lessons.scene: Yuchen is a vice president at a foreign investment bank in Shanghai, with a top-university degree and an impressive CV. This week he joins his church's workplace small group for the first time. When it is his turn to introduce himself, he notices that next to him are a delivery rider and an engineer who has just lost his job. The string of titles is already on the tip of his tongue.
q: Who is God? — Paul speaks of “the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus.” Why is Christ worth being called the treasure?
Who am I? — What sits in the asset column of your heart that you would least like to write off as loss?
How shall I respond? — If you were Yuchen, how would you introduce yourself?
lessons.jesus: Jesus held the highest CV in the universe: equal with the Father, the one through whom all things were made. Yet he gladly set it all aside, was born in a manger and grew up in Nazareth. He counted us more precious than his own honour. Because he treated us as his treasure, we can treat him as ours.
lessons.pray: Christ Jesus my Lord, you are my treasure. I confess that I often cling to job titles, degrees and other people's opinions as if they were my worth. Rework the books of my heart and put you first. Today help me use the gifts you have given me to serve people, not to raise myself up. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: List your three most valued work assets and pray over them
Ask advice from a colleague more junior than you today
Introduce yourself by whose you are before what you do
lessons.noon: “the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus, my Lord” — Lord, right now I write you back into the first column of my heart.

lessons.title: The Day They Took My Pass
lessons.theme: When I lose my position, I still belong to God

v: Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshipped.
He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the LORD’s name.”
In all this, Job didn’t sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.
Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day.
For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory,
while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.

lessons.still: Touch your staff pass, your keys or your work phone. Say to the Lord: “Lord, one day I will hand all these back, but I will always belong to you. Today I am safe in your hands.”
teach: In a single day Job lost his property, his servants and his children. His response is staggering. He tore his robe, fell to the ground and said, “Naked I came out of my mother's womb, and naked will I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the LORD's name.” Job was not without pain; tearing his robe and shaving his head were signs of deep grief. But in his grief he did not stop worshipping. He knew his identity lay not in what he owned but in the God who gives and takes away.

On your last day, HR asks you to hand in your staff pass. That little card opened the doors, the meeting rooms and the car park. Once it is handed in, the doors no longer open for you. People who are made redundant, demoted or retired often say, “When I handed in my pass, it felt as if I handed in myself.” If my identity is printed on a staff pass, losing my job means losing myself. If my identity is written on God's heart, then even without a position I am still his child.

Paul says, “though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day,” because “the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.” A job title is seen; our identity in Christ is unseen. 321 says: keep your focus on Jesus, not on your circumstances. Redundancy, demotion and retirement are real losses. They call for grief, and for the support of family, church and, where needed, professional help. But beneath it all there is an identity that is never handed back: I belong to God, and he is with me.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Shift your perspective from the temporary to the eternal. Keep your focus on Jesus, not on your circumstances. A position can be taken away, but being a child of God can never be made redundant.
lessons.scene: Ah Kun has worked as a master printer at a print shop in Kuala Lumpur for twenty-eight years. Last week the company brought in new machines and he received his redundancy notice. It is seven on Monday morning. Out of habit he has dressed and is standing at the front door before he remembers he no longer has a job to go to. His wife looks out at him from the kitchen.
q: Who is God? — “The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away.” What kind of Lord does this show God to be in your work?
Who am I? — If you handed in your pass tomorrow, how would you describe who you are?
How shall I respond? — If you were Ah Kun's wife, friend or small-group leader, how would you walk with him through this morning?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was crucified, his clothes were divided, his disciples scattered and his name was trampled. He lost everything on earth. Yet he still called God Father and committed his spirit into the Father's hands. The resurrection morning proved that the one who lost everything had never lost the Father's love.
lessons.pray: Lord who gives and takes away, I place my job, my position and my future in your hands. If one day I lose this job, remind me that I am still your child. Today I also pray for brothers and sisters facing unemployment, career change or retirement: let them find security in you. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Write: “Without this job, I am still God's child”
Send a caring message today to a friend between jobs
Pray for anyone at work recently moved on or let go
lessons.noon: “though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day” — Lord, right now I rest my identity in your eternal hands.

lessons.title: The Name on the Luggage Tag
lessons.theme: From “what I do” to “whose I am”

v: But now the LORD who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burnt, and flame will not scorch you.
For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Saviour. I have given Egypt as your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
Since you have been precious and honoured in my sight, and I have loved you, therefore I will give people in your place, and nations instead of your life.
Or don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own,
for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s.

lessons.still: Say your own name once, then hear the Lord say to you: “I have called you by your name. You are mine.” Answer him: “Lord, I am yours. Today my work is yours too.”
teach: In Isaiah 43 God speaks to his people in exile: “Don't be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.” At that time Israel had no nation, no temple and no achievements to speak of, yet God said, “you have been precious and honoured in my sight.” Paul reminds the Corinthians: “You are not your own, for you were bought with a price.” The deepest foundation of identity is not what I do but whom I belong to.

On the airport carousel, thousands of black suitcases look exactly the same. What tells them apart is not colour or brand but the tag bearing the owner's name. We often identify ourselves by our work: I'm an engineer, a nurse, a business owner, a homemaker. But work is like the style of the suitcase. It changes, gets worn and breaks. Only the name on the tag stays the same. The gospel says your tag reads: belongs to Jesus, bought with a price.

Moving from “what I do” to “whose I am” sums up this week: I am already accepted; I have died and risen with Christ; Christ is my treasure; even without a position I belong to God. 321 says change your thinking and your life changes, and when your life changes your living changes. When I know whose I am, I don't need to fight at work to prove myself, nor do I need to reject myself when I fail. I am “a people for God's own possession” (1 Peter 2:9), and so my work becomes worship.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your thinking and your life changes; change your life and your living changes. When I know whose I am, I can live the self-emptied life — not working for myself, but letting Jesus receive all the glory wherever I serve.
lessons.scene: Tama is a building foreman in Rotorua. Three months ago he fell from scaffolding and injured his leg, and he still can't return to site. At a friend's barbecue at the weekend, someone he has just met asks casually, “So, what do you do?” Everyone turns to look at him.
q: Who is God? — God says, “I have called you by your name. You are mine.” What does this show you about how God sees you?
Who am I? — If you couldn't introduce yourself by your job, what words would you use to say who you are?
How shall I respond? — If you were Tama, how would you answer when everyone turns to look?
lessons.jesus: When people asked Jesus who he was, he never answered with an occupation. He always pointed to his relationship with the Father: “I and the Father are one” (John 10:30). And with his own precious blood he wrote his name on our tags. We were bought with a price, and the price was himself.
lessons.pray: Lord who redeemed me, thank you for calling me by name and saying I am yours. I confess that I often define myself by my job, my income and my title. Today help me remember that I was bought with a price. Whatever I do, and whether or not I can work, may I glorify you in my body. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Write one sentence on whose you are, with no job titles
Tell a family member or colleague: “You matter to me”
Pick the verse that moved you most this week and memorise it
lessons.noon: “I have called you by your name. You are mine.” — Lord, right now I am not defined by my work; I am yours.

mem.t: Commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall succeed.

lessons.title: A Branch of the Kingdom
lessons.theme: May God's Kingdom come in my department as it is in heaven

v: Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us today our daily bread.
Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’

lessons.still: Before you walk into your office or workplace, pause at the door. Pray in your heart: “Father in heaven, let your Kingdom come here; let your will be done in this department as it is in heaven.” Then push the door open.
teach: When the disciples asked Jesus to teach them to pray, he gave them a remarkably simple pattern. It does not begin with our needs but with God's name, God's Kingdom and God's will: “may your name be kept holy. Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.” Only then come daily bread, forgiveness and protection. The closing doxology gathers everything back to him: “For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever.” The Lord's Prayer is itself an ordering chart for letting God be King.

Large companies have branches in many places. Headquarters' culture, standards and values are meant to land in every branch, so that customers walking into any one of them meet the same quality. “Let your Kingdom come” asks that the culture of heaven's headquarters land on earth. Your department, your shop floor, your classroom, your ward is a branch of the Kingdom. You may not be the branch manager, but you work there, and the values of the Kingdom can begin at your desk.

Praying the Lord's Prayer at work can be very concrete. “May your name be kept holy”: today my words will not shame your name. “Let your Kingdom come”: today fairness, honesty and kindness rule here. “Our daily bread”: today's orders and salary are your provision. “Forgive us our debts”: I choose to forgive that colleague. “Bring us not into temptation”: keep me from falsifying the accounts. 321 says: let Jesus be King and build God's order. It begins with prayer.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Two core convictions — let Jesus be King and let Jesus receive all the glory; one purpose — build God's order. The Lord's Prayer begins with God's Kingdom and ends with “yours is the glory”; it is 321 in the form of a prayer.
lessons.scene: Xiaofeng is a production supervisor at an electronics factory in Shenzhen. Two team leaders in his department have undermined each other for months, and the morning briefings are tense. This morning, standing at the whiteboard to begin, he sees them sitting at opposite ends of the table again, and on his phone is a message from his boss demanding that someone be held accountable.
q: Who is God? — The prayer ends with “yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory.” What place does that give God in your workplace?
Who am I? — If your department is a branch of the Kingdom, what is your role there?
How shall I respond? — If you were Xiaofeng, how could today's briefing let God's Kingdom come first?
lessons.jesus: Jesus did not only teach the Lord's Prayer; his whole life was that prayer lived out. He honoured the Father's name, announced that the Kingdom had come near, prayed in Gethsemane, “not my will, but yours, be done,” and forgave sins from the cross. In him, the Kingdom of heaven truly came to earth.
lessons.pray: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. Let your Kingdom come in my department; let your will be done at my desk as it is in heaven. Give me today my daily bread and a heart to forgive my colleagues. Keep me from temptation, for yours is the Kingdom, the power and the glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Pray the Lord's Prayer silently at the door before you go in
Practise fairness, honesty or kindness in one small matter
Pray specifically for one difficult person in your team
lessons.noon: “Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.” — Lord, right now be King in my department.

lessons.title: Recalculating Route
lessons.theme: I plan with care, commit my work, and let God direct my steps

v: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from the LORD.
All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the motives.
Commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall succeed.
A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD directs his steps.

lessons.still: Open today's calendar and run your finger gently from the first item to the last. Say to the Lord: “Lord, I commit my deeds to you. These are my plans; please direct my steps.”
teach: Proverbs 16 has several sayings that echo one another: “The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from the LORD.” “All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the motives.” This week's memory verse says, “Commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall succeed.” And verse 9: “A man's heart plans his course, but the LORD directs his steps.” Scripture does not oppose planning; we are meant to think ahead and prepare. But the final word belongs to God.

Anyone who drives with satnav knows the experience. You enter a destination and it calculates the best route. Then a road ahead is suddenly closed, and the voice says, “Recalculating route.” Our work plans are like that first route: careful, reasonable, but not the final version. The self-centred get angry at every detour, because their plan is their throne. Those who commit their way to God know that the one who directs their steps can see the closed road ahead, and his detours are often protection.

The Hebrew word behind “commit” carries the picture of rolling, like rolling a heavy load off your own shoulders onto God. This is not abandoning responsibility; it is changing who carries the weight. 321 says: let people be people and let God be God. Being human means planning wholeheartedly and giving our best. Letting God be God means leaving the outcome with him, without trying to control every variable. Working this way, we don't collapse when plans fail or boast when they succeed, because we know he directed our steps.
