lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is laying down power and returning to your place, letting people be people and God be God. I do the planning; God directs the steps. Committing my work to him is letting Jesus be King of my plans.
lessons.scene: Meifeng is a freelance designer in Taipei who has received two offers at once. One pays well but the client is notoriously difficult; the other is for a small charity with half the budget. She lays the two contracts side by side on her desk. She meant to reply by lunchtime today, but she has slept badly two nights in a row.
q: Who is God? — “The LORD directs his steps.” What role does this show God playing in your work plans?
Who am I? — When your plans are disrupted, what is your first reaction, and what does it reveal about who is king?
How shall I respond? — If you were Meifeng, how could you commit this decision to God before replying?
lessons.jesus: Jesus' life had a clear direction: towards Jerusalem and the cross. Yet his days were constantly interrupted, stopped by the sick, surrounded by children, misunderstood by his disciples. He was never flustered, because his steps were always directed by the Father; he often withdrew to quiet places to pray and receive the next step.
lessons.pray: Lord who directs my steps, I commit all of today's plans to you. I will do my best, but keep me from making my plans my throne. If you recalculate my route, give me peace to accept it. In every choice, weigh my motives and lead me in your will. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Write “Committed to the LORD” at the top of today's plan
When plans change, say: “Lord, you recalculate the route”
Write down your thinking on a stuck decision and pray over it
lessons.noon: “A man's heart plans his course, but the LORD directs his steps.” — Lord, right now I hand you my next step.

lessons.title: The Pre-Flight Checklist
lessons.theme: Ask every day: who is king today?

v: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the LORD.

lessons.still: Sit up straight in your seat and close your eyes for ten seconds. Ask yourself one question: “Who is king today?” Then say to the Lord: “Search me, God, and know my heart.”
teach: In Psalm 139 David first marvels that God knows everything and is everywhere, and then ends with this prayer: “Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.” Lamentations urges the same: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the LORD.” Self-examination is not for self-condemnation but for returning. Its destination is always God.

Before every flight, the captain and first officer work through a checklist item by item: fuel, instruments, flaps, communications. However many thousands of hours they have flown, experienced pilots never skip it, because one small oversight could bring down the whole aircraft. The spiritual life also needs a pre-flight checklist. It doesn't have to be long. One core question will do: who is king today? Is it me, my emotions, my boss, my targets, or Jesus?

321's daily “Who is king today?” check can happen at three points. In the morning before take-off: hand the day to the Lord. At midday while cruising: watch for the five faces of the self. In the evening after landing: review where Jesus was King today and where I grabbed the controls back. This is the practice, review, correction and repetition of the eight steps for changing our thinking. It is not done once; it is practised daily until it becomes a habit of life.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The eight steps for changing our thinking are information, revelation, conviction, practice, review, correction, repetition and multiplication. A daily check walks through practice, review, correction and repetition, so that new thinking grows into new life.
lessons.scene: Daryl is a systems engineer at a logistics company in Singapore. This afternoon the warehouse system went down for two hours, and the whole company is asking why. He knows it was a setting he changed yesterday, but colleagues have already started suspecting the outsourced vendor. His manager calls him into the meeting room to explain.
q: Who is God? — “Search me, God.” What kind of God meets us in the depths of our hearts like this?
Who am I? — So far today, who do you think has been king in your heart?
How shall I respond? — If you were Daryl, which item should he tick on his checklist before he walks into that room?
lessons.jesus: Jesus' prayer in Gethsemane was the most honest self-surrender: “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done” (Luke 22:42). He laid his own will before the Father and chose to let the Father be King.
lessons.pray: God who searches the heart, shine your light on every thought I have today. If there is pride, blame-shifting or a desire to control in me, show me and forgive me. At every key moment today, remind me to ask who is king. Lead me in the everlasting way. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Ask morning, noon and night: “Who is king today?”
Before bed, note one moment when Jesus was King today
Own up to a mistake straight away, before anyone finds it
lessons.noon: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the LORD.” — Lord, right now I stop and let you search my heart.

lessons.title: Stop Computing It All Locally
lessons.theme: Rely on the Holy Spirit with your heart, not on yourself with your head

v: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts.
If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.

lessons.still: Take a deep breath and rest your hands, unclenched, on the desk. Say to the Lord: “Holy Spirit, today I won't lean on my own understanding. I trust you with all my heart; please lead every step.”
teach: Proverbs says, “Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don't lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.” Zechariah records God's word to Zerubbabel: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit.” Paul goes further: “If we live by the Spirit, let's also walk by the Spirit.” The fruit of the Spirit — love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness and self-control — is not squeezed out by effort.

A computer can work in two ways. It can grind everything out locally: the processor hits a hundred per cent, the fan roars, the case heats up and eventually it crashes. Or it can connect to the cloud and hand the heavy computation to powerful remote servers, so that the local machine only needs a stable connection. Many Christians run everything locally at work: thinking it all through alone, carrying it all alone, worrying about it all alone, until they burn out. Relying on the Spirit with the heart means staying connected to God and letting him handle what we can't compute.

321 says: rely on the Holy Spirit with your heart, not on yourself with your head. Living from the heart brings joy; living from the head brings worry. This does not mean we stop thinking; God gave us minds to use well. It means not letting the mind be king. When we rely on ourselves with our heads, our focus is on our own ability, other people's reactions and our circumstances. When we rely on the Spirit with our hearts, our focus returns to Jesus. The 920 life means bearing the nine fruits of the Spirit in every relationship.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Rely on the Spirit with your heart, not on yourself with your head; keep your focus on Jesus, not on yourself, others or circumstances. 920: everyone I relate to is my “2”, I practise the self-emptied “0”, and by the Spirit I bear the “9” fruits.
lessons.scene: Bingzhong is a case officer at a district office in Kaohsiung. Just before lunch, a member of the public whose benefit application was rejected starts shouting at the counter, and everyone in the queue is watching. Bingzhong feels his blood pressure rising, and he already has three lines ready that would put the man in his place.
q: Who is God? — “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit.” What role does this show the Holy Spirit playing in your work?
Who am I? — At work, do you more often rely on yourself with your head or on the Spirit with your heart? When is it most obvious?
How shall I respond? — If you were Bingzhong, how could he walk by the Spirit in that moment?
lessons.jesus: Jesus began his ministry full of the Holy Spirit, was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, and by the Spirit drove out demons and healed the sick. He is the Son of God, yet in his days on earth he showed us a human life lived in complete dependence on the Spirit. He has given the same Spirit to us so that we can live this way too.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, I confess that I often push on with my own cleverness, and the more I think the more anxious I become. Fill me today. When I face complaints, pressure and conflict, produce in me the fruit of patience, gentleness and self-control. Let me rely not on might, nor on power, but on you. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: When emotions rise, pray silently: “Spirit, lead me”
Say one deliberately gentle word to a difficult person today
Before leaving work, pick one fruit of the Spirit to pray for tomorrow
lessons.noon: “If we live by the Spirit, let's also walk by the Spirit.” — Lord, right now I set aside my own cleverness and rely on your Spirit.

lessons.title: Release Notes for My Thinking
lessons.theme: Reviewing the thinking stage: I used to think… now I know…

v: Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.
Brothers, I don’t regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do: forgetting the things which are behind and stretching forward to the things which are before,
I press on towards the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

lessons.still: Take out a notebook or open a note on your phone. Say to the Lord: “Lord, these eight weeks you have been renewing my mind. Help me review honestly, and carry me on towards the goal.” Write today's date.
teach: Paul writes, “Don't be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.” A renewed mind is where a changed life begins. He also says, “one thing I do: forgetting the things which are behind and stretching forward to the things which are before, I press on towards the goal.” Looking back is not dwelling in the past; it is so that we can move forward more clearly. Over these eight weeks we have completed the “thinking” stage: seeing work as God's design and calling, seeing the self-centred life at work, and learning to let Jesus be King.

Every time your phone updates its system, it comes with release notes: which bugs have been fixed, which features have been added. Today, write release notes for your own thinking. For example: “I used to think work was just a way to earn a living; now I know I work alongside God.” “I used to think success proved my worth; now I know I am already accepted.” “I used to think I could be king; now I know pride is leaving my place.” The more specific you are, the more real the update.

Among 321's eight steps, review and correction are what make new thinking land. Review through the five areas of change. Thinking: has my view of work changed? Life: have the five faces of the self faded? Living: has my order of priorities shifted? Relationships: have I been the first to bow my head? Ministry: does my department look more like a branch of the Kingdom? Finally, open the Workplace Health Self-Assessment in the app and answer honestly. Success is not proof and failure is not condemnation; this is simply the starting line for the next stage.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your thinking and your life changes; change your life and your living changes. In the eight steps, review and correction turn information into revelation and revelation into life; the five changes from the inside out begin with our thinking.
lessons.scene: Cuiling teaches at a primary school in Ipoh and has done this workplace course every day on the way to school for eight weeks. Tonight she opens the Workplace Health Self-Assessment in the app and reaches the item: “I can be genuinely glad when a colleague succeeds.” She remembers the sourness she felt last week when a colleague was named Model Teacher, and her finger hovers between “Often” and “Sometimes”.
q: Who is God? — Looking back over eight weeks, in which lesson did God most help you know him afresh?
Who am I? — Complete the sentence: “I used to think… now I know…”
How shall I respond? — If you were Cuiling, which answer would she choose? Will you be that honest in your own self-assessment?
lessons.jesus: After his resurrection, beside the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus asked Peter three times whether he loved him (John 21:15–17). He was not raking up the past; he was helping Peter face the truth honestly and start again. Jesus' reviews are always full of grace. He sends the one who failed out again: “Feed my sheep.”
lessons.pray: Lord who renews my mind, thank you for these eight weeks of helping me see work, myself and you in a new way. I confess that some of my thinking has only just begun to change, and in some places I still want to be king. Help me review honestly, without self-condemnation or self-congratulation. Carry me on, forgetting what is behind and pressing on towards your goal. In the name of the Lord Jesus, Amen.
acts: Write three “I used to think… now I know…” sentences
Complete the Workplace Health Self-Assessment honestly in the app
Share your review with a spiritual companion and ask for prayer
lessons.noon: “be transformed by the renewing of your mind” — Lord, right now I give you these eight weeks of renewal. Carry me forward.
